item.title: Four Weeks, Thousands of Stories: How PalmPay’s Purple December Took Over Nigeria’s Festive Timeline
item.description: What began on December 1 as an invitation to celebrate the end of the year soon grew into something more layered. Not just a campaign, but a shared experience - one many Nigerians leaned into as the year wound down.

item.title: GridLocked 16 January 2026
item.description: The GridLocked for 15 January 2026 is food. How many tiles will you need to flip before you correctly guess?

item.title: Marriage Diaries: The Wife Figuring Out Life With a People Pleaser Husband
item.description: Ezinne* (35) never imagined marriage as something she would ease into. Even while dating the man she eventually married, she stayed alert and watched out for signs that her freedom would slip away. In this week’s Marriage Diaries, she talks about entering marriage with her guard up and learning to cope with a partner who puts everybody first.

item.title: A Letter From Zikoko's Editor
item.description: 2025 was a banner year for Zikoko. We broke records, launched new formats and hosted first-of-their-kind events. This is our plan for 2026.

item.title: “My Friends Think I’m Stingy, but I’m Just Broke” – 4 Women on Not Being Able to Keep Up Financially | Zikoko!
item.description: In this article, four Nigerian women open up about how it feels being the broke friend, and lies they tell to hide their financial struggle.

item.title: “I Chased A Perfect CGPA, But It’s Not Valued in the US” — Abroad Life
item.description: Bolaji* (24) moved to the US as a teenager without a plan except his father’s vision of him “making it” abroad. In this story, he shares his experiences and how chasing a perfect CGPA was not as fulfilling as he thought it would be.

item.title: How These 11 Nigerian Women are Monetising Their Hobbies | Zikoko!
item.description: For many Nigerian women, hobbies that began as boredom cures, coping mechanisms, or pure joy have slowly turned into income streams.

item.title: I Almost Lost My Marriage Trying to Be a Better Provider
item.description: “I made the hard decision to quit my teaching job and open an internet cafe. The money was better, and I could save toward a wedding and rent. Esther said she didn’t care about money, but that only made me determined to give her a good life.” David* (43) reflects on how he almost lost his marriage due to external pressure and pride. He shares how choosing to be vulnerable and honest with his wife helped to rebuild their love from scratch.

item.title: Why Is Everyone Obsessed With Their Wedding Going Viral?
item.description: Weddings are no longer just intimate celebrations of love; they must also feature ostentatious displays of wealth.

item.title: My Best Friend’s Betrayal Ruined Our Friendship
item.description: Kunle* (42) thought his friendship with his best friend, Jimi* (42), would last forever until one incident in 2003 changed everything. In this edition of Sunken Ships, Kunle shares how their bond was built, what broke it, and how that moment reshaped the way he views friendships.
